why: The <<expr=result>> form teaches 'write the expression then the result' -- one continuous generation. An agent loop needs 'write the call then STOP', with the result given. Opposite behaviours on identical content; the single-span form trains a model that fabricates its own tool outputs.

task: context length: per-position loss curve within 4096 and behaviour beyond it, on ckpt_p324
why: NoPE means there is no RoPE to extrapolate; the 3 gated-MLA layers are full causal and the 9 KDA layers carry a fixed-size state, so the two halves may behave oppositely past the training length. Nobody has measured it, and an agent loop is the first thing that will hit it.
reading: smooth rise past 4096 => usable but degrading, fixable by training length. Cliff at 4096 => a hard bound, and the agent loop must close inside it -- a design constraint on 30B. Also: if loss rises within 4096, the usable context is shorter than the nominal one and THAT is the number that matters.

task: e1-19's manifest restore was positional: it fired at the two exits that existed below the write, and the manifest stage happens to be the last stage, so those were all the exits. Make the cleanup structural -- armed at the write, disarmed only when the hook approves the commit -- so a gate added later cannot reopen the livelock.
why: Self-caught while checking what e1-19 did NOT cover. Appending one hypothetical gate after the manifest stage brought the residue back and with it b0's three-way lock, without touching the manifest code at all. A cleanup whose correctness depends on nothing being added after it is a trap for whoever adds the next gate, and this file's history is gates being added.

evidence: scripts/hooks/pre-commit: _MANIFEST_RESTORE armed immediately before the --write-index call, popped at the LAST LINE of main(), executed by an atexit handler, so every exit between the write and approval is covered including ones not yet written. The disarm's placement is the fix and my first draft got it wrong: I put it beside the `git add` that stages the manifest, which reads natural and is not -- STAGING IS NOT APPROVAL, a gate refusing after the manifest stage still aborts the commit and a guard disarmed at the `git add` is already down by then. World 10 stayed red under that draft and I established whether the world or the fix was wrong before changing either. World 10 (new) needs a MUTATED copy of the hook since the future gate does not exist yet; it injects at the disarm line and NOT at the adjacent 'hook: total' print, because a gate below the disarm is outside the guarded region by construction and anchoring there tests the fixture rather than the design -- and if the anchor is not found exactly once the world reports 'untested' instead of passing. Worlds 7-9 cannot separate the two designs at all: with the manifest stage last there is no exit between the write and the end for them to probe, which is why e1-19 read green. task: e1-19's manifest restore was positional: it fired at the two exits that existed below the write, and the manifest stage happens to be the last stage, so those were all the exits. Make the cleanup structural -- armed at the write, disarmed only when the hook approves the commit -- so a gate added later cannot reopen the livelock.
why: Self-caught while checking what e1-19 did NOT cover. Appending one hypothetical gate after the manifest stage brought the residue back and with it b0's three-way lock, without touching the manifest code at all. A cleanup whose correctness depends on nothing being added after it is a trap for whoever adds the next gate, and this file's history is gates being added.
reading: pre-commit --selftest green at 10 worlds, with world 10 red under e1-19's own design.
evidence: scripts/hooks/pre-commit: _MANIFEST_RESTORE armed immediately before the --write-index call, popped at the LAST LINE of main(), executed by an atexit handler, so every exit between the write and approval is covered including ones not yet written. The disarm's placement is the fix and my first draft got it wrong: I put it beside the `git add` that stages the manifest, which reads natural and is not -- STAGING IS NOT APPROVAL, a gate refusing after the manifest stage still aborts the commit and a guard disarmed at the `git add` is already down by then. World 10 stayed red under that draft and I established whether the world or the fix was wrong before changing either. World 10 (new) needs a MUTATED copy of the hook since the future gate does not exist yet; it injects at the disarm line and NOT at the adjacent 'hook: total' print, because a gate below the disarm is outside the guarded region by construction and anchoring there tests the fixture rather than the design -- and if the anchor is not found exactly once the world reports 'untested' instead of passing. evidence: scripts/harness.py: the permanent red was git's auto-scaling sha abbreviation, not a stale assertion. _selftest_merge_reverted_content compared at == 'd5aac3d' against a value from git log --format=%h; %h auto-scales with the object count when core.abbrev is unset, so d5aac3d printed as 7 chars when de-22 wrote the assertion and as 8 (d5aac3d5) once the repository crossed the next threshold. THE TASK'S OWN DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG and in a costly direction: it said recent merge commits changed the inheritance shape and the assertion went stale, but merge_reverted_content still classifies c8a4578 exactly as designed (_built_set, taken from theirs, already dropped by d5aac3d) -- only the printed WIDTH of the answer moved, and acting on the task's reading would have meant re-deriving inheritance logic that was never broken. FIXED AT THE PRODUCER, NOT THE ASSERTION: merge_reverted_content now returns %H, the full 40-char sha, because already_dropped_at is an identity handed to callers and an identity whose text depends on repository size is not one; fixing only the assertion would leave the next caller to rediscover this. The other %h in that function (scripts/harness.py:2713) is tested for truthiness only and is unaffected. The assertion now tests the fact it means -- startswith('d5aac3d'), which names the commit without depending on how git printed it -- PLUS a length assertion, because startswith alone is satisfied by the very abbreviation this commit removes, so without it the same time bomb could be reintroduced at the producer with the selftest staying green. task: one mixer.o per run collapses to 42-70% of the median layer norm, and the layer is not predictable: find why, and whether it costs anything. The differentiator is the angle between the orthogonalised Muon update and the weight -- cos(orth(mb),W) is -0.0259 at the collapsed layer vs -0.056..-0.067 everywhere else (2.4x less anti-aligned). The cautious-decay mask rate is NOT the differentiator (0.4788-0.4815 across all 12 layers, 0.56% spread). Next unmeasured step: whether the system is at equilibrium at all -- the equilibrium of train.py:592 predicts a ratio of 0.410 and the measurement is 0.523, off by 28%, and a system still moving would explain that.
why: three completed runs each have exactly one such layer (15b_s1 L10 at 42% of median, p200m_4b L9 at 70%, data_leg_206m L9 at 53%), all three at seed 42 and attn_every 4. So 'which layer' is not set by the seed, the architecture position, or initialisation, but 'one layer does' happens every time. That shape points at a symmetry breaking during training, decided by data order.
reading: either a mechanism that predicts WHICH layer collapses, or a measurement showing the collapse costs nothing (val/domain_loss indistinguishable with and without it). Ruled out already, with the counter-evidence: initialisation (all 12 layers 20.47-20.49 at seed 42, the collapsed layer among them), A_log runaway (L0 max +7.84 and L1 +7.16 are MORE extreme than L9's +3.70 while their mixer.o is normal at 57.66/55.21), dt_bias (L9 -16.375, inside the -10.9..-17.0 range), and the cautious mask.

evidence: ||mb|| at the collapsed layer is 0.0294-0.0304, 28x the median 0.0011 and 6.6x the second-highest of 63 Muon matrices, and blocks.9.mixer.qkv is 5th -- the whole mixer is receiving large consistent gradients. mb is an EMA (train.py:578, momentum 0.95), so a large norm means CONSISTENT gradient direction, not sign flipping; and the update is orthogonalised (train.py:579-590) so its displacement is set by shape, not by ||mb|| -- 6e's correction of my first reading, which had it backwards both ways. Index mapping verified by shape before reading any number: 63 mb tensors compared against their weights, zero mismatches. The relative gap over three checkpoints is 0.5256 (6500) -> 0.5134 (7000) -> 0.5229 (8000): NOT monotone, so the -2.33%/1000 step rate rests on two points and the third did not continue it. Those checkpoints survive only because they were hardlink-pinned as milestone_earlyanchor_step7000/7500 -- the newest-3 roller had already deleted step6000 and step6500 within 20 minutes of their being read, and with them the only comparison that holds recipe, data, seed and hardware fixed.

reading: The safety is a property of the DIFF, not of the flag: the override was safe for de-47 because all 1666 added bytes land after 4391, and the same flag on an edit touching byte 4000 would be unsafe with no warning at all. A third fixture for the zombie: a pid whose /proc exists with no fds must not read as 'nothing is running'. Namespace rule applies -- pids and fdinfo must be read in the SAME view, the container's, since ~/bin/pod's pgrep and /proc agree only there

task: card_claim.claims() must ask _is_zombie as its own docstring instructs: a Z pid makes the claim STALE (cards reclaimable, released with a note), and card_held_without_claim names a stale claim in its WARN instead of saying 'no claim'
why: MEASURED with a real zombie (a child that exits under a parent that never reaps it, ps -o stat= reads Z): _alive(pid)=True, _is_zombie(pid)=True, claims() returns live=['zjob'] stale=[], held_cards=['5']. So a FINISHED-BUT-UNREAPED job's claim reads LIVE and its cards stay held forever. card_claim._alive()'s own docstring already states the trap -- 'True for a ZOMBIE: see _is_zombie. Callers that mean is-the-job-running must ask both' -- and claims() is a caller that means exactly that and asks only _alive. _is_zombie exists and returns the right answer; nothing calls it here. THIS ROW REPLACES A REFUTED ONE. I first reported the opposite (claims() DROPS a zombie's claim) from an empty runs/claims/ -- and the directory was empty because b0 released both claims between my two probes, which I read as a reader dropping rows. The refuted direction is recorded here so it is not rediscovered: a zombie claim is not dropped, it is never released
reading: The fix inverts the direction I first reported, so the selftest is the real-zombie fixture rather than a hand-written pid: spawn an unreaped child, write a claim naming it, and assert live=[] stale=['zjob'] with the card NOT in held_cards. A hand-written pid cannot produce state Z, and a fixture that cannot reach the state under test asserts nothing. Positive beside it: a genuinely running pid's claim must stay LIVE and keep holding its card, without which the fix is indistinguishable from treating every claim as stale -- which would hand out cards under live jobs, strictly worse than the bug. Second half unchanged from 6e's original text and still right: the WARN should read 'card 0: claim b0_sd_unlooped stale (pid Z)' rather than 'no claim', because 'no claim' and 'a claim whose job ended' call for different actions
evidence: scripts/harness.py check_card_held_without_claim separates zombie-held cards from unclaimed ones and names the claim, pid, Z state and release command; scripts/card_claim.py claims() docstring records why a zombie is deliberately not stale

why: sft_math.py:111-115 defaults grad_ckpt=True (comment at :207 claims FP8 backward NaNs without it, uncited) and model.py:1230 refuses moe_experts with grad_ckpt, so sft_math cannot load a MoE checkpoint AT ITS DEFAULTS. At ratio 1 either side can be in its tail, so an annealing arm against a stable comparator would have gone unflagged. Both arms share total 10,172 and warmdown 9155, so no pair is mixed BY CONSTRUCTION -- which is what makes the mixed count a check on that construction rather than noise: non-zero means the totals diverged. task: pod_pull_ledgers --push cannot send a value-only correction: give sig() a whole-row fallback for ledgers with no status/result/ended field
why: MEASURED 2026-09-06 on the real ledgers. I appended a unit correction to runs/milestones.jsonl (matchedtok_step5000: actual_tokens 3.93 in BILLIONS -> 3932160000 raw, aligning the one row that deviated from the 13 others), committed it, merged to main (1a7b51b8), then ran --push. It reported `runs/milestones.jsonl pod 12 local 16 local-only 0` and `no local-only rows: every key on one side is present on the other`. The pod still held one row under that key and its consumer still read 3.93. ROOT CAUSE at pod_pull_ledgers.py:353-355: events_pod_lacks identifies an event as (keyfn, status, result, ended). No milestones row carries status, result or ended, so the old and the corrected row produce the byte-identical signature ((ckpt, milestone), '', '', ''), the correction is judged the SAME event, `missing` never offers it and collisions are never applied. The report is true and answers a different question than the one asked: it answers whether key coverage is complete, not whether the pod's current value is right. New keys can be pushed; a close can be pushed (a close changes status, so the signature moves -- that is what de-41 built events_pod_lacks for); a value-only correction cannot. For milestones, moe_diag and memory_diag, which have no status field at all, the push direction is blind to every value correction. No workaround exists outside this tool by design: pod_push.sh:245 excludes runs/ from the file push so a whole-file overwrite cannot destroy rows the pod wrote since the last sync, and podput of a tracked file is banned (the pod has no git).
produces: pod_pull_ledgers.py: sig() falls back to a whole-row signature for ledgers whose rows carry none of status/result/ended, so a changed payload is a distinct event and reachable by --push. Two DIFFERENT non-empty values on the two sides still classify as `contradicts` and are left for a human -- the fallback must widen what can be SENT, not what can be overwritten. Selftest broken world built from the two real milestones rows (3.93 and 3932160000 under one key): it must FAIL before the fix and PASS after, and a negative control must show the fallback does NOT fire on a ledger that does have status.
decides: Whether a value correction made on main can reach the pod at all, for every ledger with no status field. Today it cannot, and --push reports success.

task: card_claim.py acquire --wait-for-device cannot claim a job shorter than its poll interval, so a short measurement runs on a granted card with NOTHING in the claim ledger. Observed 2026-09-07: b0-27's post-fix run (~20s, two forward+backward passes on a 4-block model) exited before the poller found a descendant on a card, and card_claim printed 'pid 2073457 exited while --wait-for-device was polling, so it never had a descendant on a card. Nothing was claimed.' The measurement completed and read 1.0000 -- correct numbers, zero claim -- and a peer reading nvidia-smi and the ledger at 00:5xZ correctly saw an idle card with no claim while the run had already happened. Fix the shape, not that one run: --wait-for-device exists for a LAUNCHER following torchrun onto a card, where the job outlives the poll; a self-claiming short job needs a different mechanism. The workaround that worked is a python wrapper holding the claim in its own pid across the whole measurement (python because card_claim refuses a shell), which is 20 lines every short job must re-derive.
why: A claim ledger that a whole class of jobs silently escapes is worse than one that refuses them: idle-is-not-a-grant is enforced by reading claims, so an unclaimed run makes a card look free while it is in use, and the next session's launch is the collision. The class is not rare -- every score_matrix row, every micro-timing, every known-answer test on a card is seconds to minutes, i.e. shorter than the poll. The failure is silent in the direction that matters (it prints a note and exits 0), so nobody discovers it until two jobs land on one card.
reading: A claim is landed if runs/card_claim.json (or whatever card_claim writes) carries the job's pid and cards for the job's whole lifetime, checked by reading the ledger DURING the run rather than after -- a claim that appears and vanishes reads identically to one never written, which is the bug. Measured at three durations: ~5s, ~20s (the observed failure), and ~120s (long enough that the poller wins). Null result = the claim lands at all three and the 2026-09-07 log line came from something else, in which case the log line itself is the finding and must be explained rather than dismissed. A fix is only accepted with a FAILING case first: a job short enough to escape the current code must be shown escaping it, then shown claimed.
produces: whether card_claim.py can bind a claim to a job that exits within its poll interval, and if not, the smallest change that lets a short job claim itself: measured as the shortest job duration that reliably lands a claim, before and after
decides: if a short job cannot self-claim, either --wait-for-device gains a bind-before-launch path or card_claim grows a documented wrapper entry point that short jobs call instead of re-deriving 20 lines each; if it can and the 2026-09-07 failure was misuse, the fix is the refusal message naming the right flag rather than any code change

task: harness check main_in_no_worktree: FAIL/WARN when `git worktree list --porcelain` shows refs/heads/main checked out in any worktree. Delivered as PR #52 with a real two-plus-one worktree broken world and a dedicated selftest.
why: AGENTS.md asserted it as a property -- "main is checked out in no worktree at all, which is what makes the compare-and-swap below legal" -- and nothing verified it. It stopped being true 2026-09-08: aupai-b0 holds refs/heads/main at 47148ae3 and main was fast-forwarded there by hand (4c measured it, de reproduced it). merge_main advances main by an atomic update-ref that touches no working tree, which is safe only while no tree holds main -- a holder's index and HEAD are not updated, so the branch moves under a checkout that still believes it is at the old commit, and a `git checkout .` there discards main's own commits.
reading: A world whose only attached worktree holds main cannot tell "main is checked out" from "a branch is checked out": mutant M2 (match `branch refs/heads/` instead of `refs/heads/main`) SURVIVED the first version, and that mutant is a check which WARNs on all ten sessions' worktrees while reading as correct. So the world needs a third worktree on a non-main branch and an assertion that the WARN does not name it. A green sweep with any mutant surviving means the check is measuring worktree count or branch-attachment, not main.
produces: The mutation result: which of M1 (count worktrees), M2 (any branch), M3 (never report) reds the selftest, plus the live WARN naming the holding worktree.
decides: WARN stands if the failure mode needs main to MOVE under the holder (it does) and the fix is another session's git worktree op (it is). If a holder is ever found to corrupt a tree without main moving, the tier goes to FAIL.

task: pre-commit gate _refuse_committing_on_main: refuse a commit whose HEAD is the branch main, with scripts/test_on_main_refusal.py as its five-world test. Delivered as PR #55.
why: 4c's follow-up to tonight's loss. b0 committed 484a9528 onto refs/heads/main from aupai-b0, which had main checked out, then reset main to origin/main; the sideways move refused every commit in the repository until fb's PR #54 recorded the pair by hand. main_in_no_worktree (PR #52) sees that state statically and asks another session to fix their own tree; nothing refused the act that turns the state into a loss.
reading: 4c's proposed predicate -- HEAD is main AND main != origin/main -- would NOT have fired: at 05:40:09 local main was 7049750c and origin/main had been pushed to 7049750c at 05:39:05, so the two were EQUAL and the divergence was created BY the commit the hook runs before. A predicate reading the state a commit produces cannot see the commit that produces it. Separately, my own justification for symbolic-ref over rev-parse --abbrev-ref was FALSE: both refuse identically when detached, and the swap mutant survived all four worlds until an UNBORN HEAD was added, where abbrev-ref exits 128 and permits the repo's first commit on main.
produces: The five-world mutation result: swap symbolic-ref -> red on W2 alone; 4c's origin/main predicate -> red on W1+W2; removed call site -> red on W1+W2; dropped merge exemption -> red on W5. Plus the three hook worlds the gate broke (5c, 5e, 8) and the reason each was the world's bug: setup commits advancing main from a tree checked out on main.
decides: The gate ships on HEAD's branch name alone. If a case is ever found where a commit on main is legitimate beyond finishing a conflicted merge, the exemption widens; the origin/main clause does not come back, because the incident proves it reads zero at the moment it matters.

evidence: PR #63 merged at 851de1a9. _launch_after_row now closes the row when the wrapped command exits nonzero without ever opening a device, and the world is in _selftest_launch_closes_its_orphaned_row: rc 2 with no device closes the row, rc 0 with no device does NOT (de-47's fast eval, whose row the monitor closes). Asserted through exp.py as the writer and the ledger's own fold, never a scan for status=='running'. THE PREDICATE IS THE WRAPPER'S OWN .rc, not the absence of a claim: the wrapper writes that file itself, so its presence means the command ran to completion and its content is the verdict. Neither existing guard covered this -- the raise guard's window closed because Popen succeeded, and the monitor watches a live pid while this one had exited. THREE OF MY OWN ASSERTIONS WERE WRONG BEFORE THE SWEEP KILLED ALL THREE MUTANTS. I read inspect.getsource(cmd_launch) when the Popen half lives in _launch_after_row, so it fired on a correct fix. M3 (arm the monitor first) survived twice: first because the ordering assertion compared indexes of the bare string '_arm_monitor', so a reference inserted above the closer left the first occurrence where it was; then because the window searched was sliced FROM the closer, putting everything above it outside the slice -- a criterion cannot see what its own slice excludes, which is §268's ceiling in a new place. And the sweep's own first version copied scripts/ to a temp dir where every run including the control died on ModuleNotFoundError before reaching the test, so three mutants read 'green'; it now requires the assertion string and reports a death without one as RED-BUT-SILENT. Final sweep: M1 (remove the closer), M2 (close on rc 0 too), M3 (arm the monitor first) all RED, control green, harness.py restored byte-for-byte. task: eval/score_matrix.py and eval/domain_bpb.py must stamp the cache fingerprints they READ into their own output row: per scored domain, the srcfp/vocab/seed sidecar values beside /mnt/data02/tokens/tokens_<domain>.pt at read time.
why: A per-domain score is only comparable to another row if both read the same val rows, and val_seqs takes a seed-42 PREFIX sized 5% of the pool capped at 5000 (eval/domain_loss.py:78) -- so the rows are stable only while the cache is unchanged. Today NOTHING in a score_matrix row records which cache it read. Comparing the 8B .step9000 row (scored 09-07) against the .step34000 row (09-08) therefore rests on an inference from present-day file state, not on a stamp either run captured. 98 and I both verified the four uncapped domains are unchanged (srcfp chat_qa=42a4bedde020ae66, chatml=52a6b427818c90ff, code_py_rp1t=63c2b3ce0e7dd989, cot=388496b76ed9bf88; vocab 0bce3584bc24f255 on all four; seed 42; ctime==mtime 2026-09-05 03:49-03:54Z, predating both scorings) -- but that verification was only possible because nobody had rebuilt them. Had one been rebuilt, the two rows would have compared different val sets under the same domain name with no way to detect it after the fact. Five of nine domains sit on the 5000 cap and are insensitive; the exposure is chat_qa 442, chatml 452, code_py_rp1t 4886, cot 4925 -- and cot is also the domain carrying a 13x weight difference between the two mixes, so it is the one most likely to be read as a learning delta. CORRECTION (b0, same session): this row's first write carried socket uds:/tmp/cc-socks/39436.sock, which is TILERL's address, not mine -- b0 is uds:/tmp/cc-socks/92633.sock per runs/roster.json members[]. A wrong socket on an open task routes its reviewer's questions to the wrong session, and the row still folds as mine because the fold is on `id`, so nothing would have flagged it. Appended rather than edited: tasks.jsonl is an event log folded by id, last row wins.
produces: each score_matrix / domain_bpb output row carries a `cache_fp` map {domain: {srcfp, vocab, seed, n_val}} for every domain it scored
decides: whether two per-domain rows may be differenced at all: equal fingerprints means the val rows are identical and the delta is the model; unequal means the comparison is invalid and must say so rather than print a number
evidence: eval/domain_loss.py:78 val_seqs (n_val = min(max(1, int(len(seqs)*0.05)), 5000)); train.py:309 val_frac=0.05, train.py:391 val_rows_max=5000; the four sidecar triples above, read on the pod 2026-09-08
reading: mtime is not evidence of content -- touch, a copy or a restore all move it, and a rebuild writing identical bytes moves it while nothing about the val rows changed. ctime is stronger (it cannot be set backwards) and is what makes today's verification real, but the durable fix is a stamp captured AT READ TIME by the reader, which is the same contract eval/l1_fewshot.py's attest() already applies to its preds file.

task: harness check main_in_no_worktree: FAIL/WARN when `git worktree list --porcelain` shows refs/heads/main checked out in any worktree. Delivered as PR #52 with a real two-plus-one worktree broken world and a dedicated selftest.
why: AGENTS.md asserted it as a property -- "main is checked out in no worktree at all, which is what makes the compare-and-swap below legal" -- and nothing verified it. It stopped being true 2026-09-08: aupai-b0 holds refs/heads/main at 47148ae3 and main was fast-forwarded there by hand (4c measured it, de reproduced it). merge_main advances main by an atomic update-ref that touches no working tree, which is safe only while no tree holds main -- a holder's index and HEAD are not updated, so the branch moves under a checkout that still believes it is at the old commit, and a `git checkout .` there discards main's own commits.
reading: A world whose only attached worktree holds main cannot tell "main is checked out" from "a branch is checked out": mutant M2 (match `branch refs/heads/` instead of `refs/heads/main`) SURVIVED the first version, and that mutant is a check which WARNs on all ten sessions' worktrees while reading as correct. So the world needs a third worktree on a non-main branch and an assertion that the WARN does not name it. task: merge_main: branch the push-failure advice by cause, and refuse a stale local main
why:
scripts/merge_main.sh has two defects on one flow; they must land together because they touch the same path and would conflict as separate patches.

(A) THE PUSH-FAILURE ADVICE IS WRITTEN FOR ONE CAUSE AND PRINTED FOR ALL. Lines 1965-1969 print four lines when the push fails. This is what produced the repo-wide red on 2026-09-08: 4c followed :1966, it failed, and `git branch -f` was what looked left. A confidently wrong tool is worse than a silent one -- it gets the operator to comply, fail, and conclude they are out of moves. REFUTED CANDIDATE, do not re-propose: `git fetch origin main:main` fails in the same state (rc=128 'refusing to fetch into branch checked out at' with main checked out, rc=1 non-fast-forward without) because a refspec without `+` requires the fast-forward whose absence caused the refusal.

Verified: the string 'fetch' appears once in the whole file, inside a comment at :1951 -- there is no fetch anywhere on the path. 4c hit this the same day and the symptom is deceptive: with #108 already on origin/main, re-running merge_main took MERGE_HEAD = 12ecbf52 (their stale local main), so the working tree still held the unpatched harness.py and still FAILED -- the recovery action read a pre-fix world and the symptom pointed at the patch being wrong. Fix (tilerl's, plus 4c's addition): fetch and check behindness against origin/main before merging; REFUSE when behind and say by how many commits. Do NOT fetch silently and continue -- that only makes 'I thought I merged X and merged Y' quieter.

ACCEPTANCE, three worlds, and the second is the one that stops this becoming the same defect in the other direction:
  1. non-fast-forward: prints the new advice, and re-running merge_main actually recovers.
  2. push fails for any other reason with origin unmoved: still prints the existing four lines. Testing only world 1 re-commits the original error -- one class's advice sent to every class.
  3. local main behind origin/main: refuses and names the count; local main equal to origin/main: prints nothing.

ONE SENTENCE FOR THE FAMILY (tilerl, 2026-09-08): a stale local ref treated as authoritative. Siblings: reading a PR head's green as main's green; treating A..HEAD as including the working tree.

task: Writing standard: state the denominator of an incomplete measurement, not the attempted rate
why:
From reviewing PR #100 (98's 62-domain reproducibility table), which does this right and is the worked example. 59 of 62 domains were not_tried; the entry reports '2 of 62 proven, 59 unknown' and labels itself a LOWER BOUND, rather than '2 of 3 attempted = 67%'.

task: merge_main: branch the push-failure advice by cause, and refuse a stale local main
why:
scripts/merge_main.sh has two defects on one flow; they must land together because they touch the same path and would conflict as separate patches.

(A) THE PUSH-FAILURE ADVICE IS WRITTEN FOR ONE CAUSE AND PRINTED FOR ALL. Lines 1965-1969 print four lines when the push fails. MEASURED 2026-09-08 in a constructed integration-tree world (main a ref only, peer PR landed on origin first): for a non-fast-forward rejection, 'the merge LANDED and only delivery failed' is false (origin moved), 'Retry the push alone' returns rc=1 and never succeeds, and 'Do NOT re-run the merge' forbids THE ONLY ACTION THAT WORKS -- re-running gives rc=0, old main IS an ancestor of the new merge (so the CAS is legal and main_advances_by_ancestry stays quiet), the push then succeeds, and both sides' work survives with zero forcing commands. This is what produced the repo-wide red on 2026-09-08: 4c followed :1966, it failed, and `git branch -f` was what looked left. A confidently wrong tool is worse than a silent one -- it gets the operator to comply, fail, and conclude they are out of moves. REFUTED CANDIDATE, do not re-propose: `git fetch origin main:main` fails in the same state (rc=128 'refusing to fetch into branch checked out at' with main checked out, rc=1 non-fast-forward without) because a refspec without `+` requires the fast-forward whose absence caused the refusal.
Fix: branch on _po_err. non-fast-forward / fetch first / behind its remote -> say origin moved and to re-run `bash scripts/merge_main.sh <branch>`. Every other cause keeps the current four lines. The section-245 update-ref prohibition stays on BOTH branches.

(B) IT MERGES THE LOCAL main REF WITHOUT FETCHING. Verified: the string 'fetch' appears once in the whole file, inside a comment at :1951 -- there is no fetch anywhere on the path. 4c hit this the same day and the symptom is deceptive: with #108 already on origin/main, re-running merge_main took MERGE_HEAD = 12ecbf52 (their stale local main), so the working tree still held the unpatched harness.py and still FAILED -- the recovery action read a pre-fix world and the symptom pointed at the patch being wrong. Fix (tilerl's, plus 4c's addition): fetch and check behindness against origin/main before merging; REFUSE when behind and say by how many commits. Do NOT fetch silently and continue -- that only makes 'I thought I merged X and merged Y' quieter.

ACCEPTANCE, three worlds, and the second is the one that stops this becoming the same defect in the other direction:
  1. non-fast-forward: prints the new advice, and re-running merge_main actually recovers.
  2. push fails for any other reason with origin unmoved: still prints the existing four lines. Testing only world 1 re-commits the original error -- one class's advice sent to every class.
  3. local main behind origin/main: refuses and names the count; local main equal to origin/main: prints nothing.

ONE SENTENCE FOR THE FAMILY (tilerl, 2026-09-08): a stale local ref treated as authoritative. Siblings: reading a PR head's green as main's green; treating A..HEAD as including the working tree.

task: merge_main: branch the push-failure advice by cause, and refuse a stale local main
why:
scripts/merge_main.sh has two defects on one flow; they must land together because they touch the same path and would conflict as separate patches.

(A) THE PUSH-FAILURE ADVICE IS WRITTEN FOR ONE CAUSE AND PRINTED FOR ALL. Lines 1965-1969 print four lines when the push fails. MEASURED 2026-09-08 in a constructed integration-tree world (main a ref only, peer PR landed on origin first): for a non-fast-forward rejection, 'the merge LANDED and only delivery failed' is false (origin moved), 'Retry the push alone' returns rc=1 and never succeeds, and 'Do NOT re-run the merge' forbids THE ONLY ACTION THAT WORKS -- re-running gives rc=0, old main IS an ancestor of the new merge (so the CAS is legal and main_advances_by_ancestry stays quiet), the push then succeeds, and both sides' work survives with zero forcing commands. This is what produced the repo-wide red on 2026-09-08: 4c followed :1966, it failed, and `git branch -f` was what looked left. A confidently wrong tool is worse than a silent one -- it gets the operator to comply, fail, and conclude they are out of moves. REFUTED CANDIDATE, do not re-propose: `git fetch origin main:main` fails in the same state (rc=128 'refusing to fetch into branch checked out at' with main checked out, rc=1 non-fast-forward without) because a refspec without `+` requires the fast-forward whose absence caused the refusal.
Fix: branch on _po_err. non-fast-forward / fetch first / behind its remote -> say origin moved and to re-run `bash scripts/merge_main.sh <branch>`. Every other cause keeps the current four lines. The section-245 update-ref prohibition stays on BOTH branches.

(B) IT MERGES THE LOCAL main REF WITHOUT FETCHING. Verified: the string 'fetch' appears once in the whole file, inside a comment at :1951 -- there is no fetch anywhere on the path. 4c hit this the same day and the symptom is deceptive: with #108 already on origin/main, re-running merge_main took MERGE_HEAD = 12ecbf52 (their stale local main), so the working tree still held the unpatched harness.py and still FAILED -- the recovery action read a pre-fix world and the symptom pointed at the patch being wrong. Fix (tilerl's, plus 4c's addition): fetch and check behindness against origin/main before merging; REFUSE when behind and say by how many commits. Do NOT fetch silently and continue -- that only makes 'I thought I merged X and merged Y' quieter.

ACCEPTANCE, three worlds, and the second is the one that stops this becoming the same defect in the other direction:
  1. non-fast-forward: prints the new advice, and re-running merge_main actually recovers.
  2. push fails for any other reason with origin unmoved: still prints the existing four lines. Testing only world 1 re-commits the original error -- one class's advice sent to every class.
  3. local main behind origin/main: refuses and names the count; local main equal to origin/main: prints nothing.

ONE SENTENCE FOR THE FAMILY (tilerl, 2026-09-08): a stale local ref treated as authoritative. Siblings: reading a PR head's green as main's green; treating A..HEAD as including the working tree.
produces: the count of push-failure causes that receive advice matching their own cause: 2 of 2 (non-fast-forward, other), against 1 of 2 today
decides: whether an operator whose push is refused reaches a working recovery from the printed text alone. Today they do not, and the recorded outcome was a forced ref write that turned the whole repository red.

task: V4.1 Step 1: implement CSA2 core in a flat stack (learned entries + dedicated indexer + single concatenated softmax)
why:
WHAT: Implement CSA2 core in a FLAT stack behind a csa2 flag — Step 1 of docs/standards/v41_pivot.md (PR #210). This is the central mechanism of the new target and the first gate candidate; everything else waits on it.
WHY: user order 2026-09-10 replaced V2 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. V2 PR #206 is dead, do not merge it.
BUILD (from a full-read gap map against model.py, verified):
1. Rewrite CompressedSparseAttention (model.py:381-538). CSA2 = (a) learned non-overlapping m-token KV entries with a learned projection producing entries C and per-entry weights Z, REPLACING the mean-pool in pool_per_doc (model.py:277-318 — keep its block/visibility/per-document machinery, change only the aggregation to a learned entry); (b) a DEDICATED lightweight indexer: indexer-Q Linear from H, indexer-K Linear over the compressed entries (not H), low-dim scores -> top-k entry indices per query; (c) gather those entries and run ONE concatenated softmax over [selected entries ; local SWA window K/V]. DELETE branch_gate, the y_sel full-resolution gather, and the separate y_cmp softmax — V4.1 has no branch gate (Fig 4, Sec 2.3).
2. Reuse the existing cu per-document isolation, blk_last<=t visibility, masked_attend, and the all-masked-row handling. Extend scripts/test_arch_compat.py with causality and cross-document cases for the indexer path; indexer top-k must never select a future or cross-document entry.
3. Geometry at OUR width, do NOT copy 552B: paper uses 32 indexer-Q heads x dim 128 against 64 core heads x dim 512 at latent 1280 (Sec 4.2.1). At d=1024/h=8 derive values that divide evenly — gap-map suggestion indexer 4 heads x 64 dim, core latent d//4=256 — but put them in Cfg and record the choice; this is a Step-0 config decision and I want your numbers.
4. Start m=4..8 and top-k 64..128 for seq 4096 (paper m=2/1, top-k 512 are for 64K-1M; at 4K top-k 512 over m=8 entries is dense attention in disguise). A/B later; one value to start.
5. No CED, no Reindex, no FP4, no bounded replay in this task — flat stack only. SWA branch already exists; pure-SWA-first-two-blocks is a separate task.
GREEN: a config builds and runs a forward+backward on meta then real tensors with csa2=true; the three invariant classes (causal, per-document, finite-on-all-masked-row) pass; a dedicated test proves the indexer mask cannot leak future/cross-doc entries. Reference is the paper text in docs/standards/v41_pivot.md and the PDF at /Users/bytedance/Downloads/DeepSeek_V41_Tech_Report.pdf Sec 2.3.
reading: green only if: the indexer selection is independently mask-tested against future and cross-document leakage; learned entries replace mean-pool rather than wrapping it; exactly one softmax runs over the concatenated key set; and every new knob is a Cfg field the frozen-config path can see (the failure the unmerged #206 was built to avoid)
produces: a csa2-flagged attention module whose forward+backward passes causal/per-document tests, with m, indexer geometry and top-k in Cfg
decides: whether the V4.1 gate model has its KV-compression core; Steps 2-5 and the first gate run all build on this

why:
WHAT: V4.1 Step 0 — freeze the small-scale CSA2 config as Cfg fields before de builds the module (de-103). No model math, a sizing deliverable.
WHY: user order 2026-09-10 replaced V2 with DeepSeek-V4.1. Your ae-1 tokenizer task is paused (model-independent, resumes later). The paper gives hyperparameters only for a 552B / 64-head / latent-1280 / seq-64K model; none of them transfer numerically to d=1024, h=8, seq 4096, ~350M. They must be re-derived so checkpoints carry them.
PRODUCE, as numbers with the arithmetic shown, written into Cfg defaults and a scripts/v41_size.py that builds on the existing p1_size.py:
1. Total layers L for ~350M active, and (for the later CED A/B) the encoder/decoder split. Gap-map suggestion L=12; verify against the active-param budget with the MoE kept at 48/top-3/1-shared/expert_ffn-768 and attn at d=1024,h=8.
2. CSA2 layer mode map for a FLAT stack: how many Full vs Reuse layers and their spacing. Paper encoder = 3 groups of [1 Full + 5 Reuse] over 18 layers, decoder different; at ~10 attention layers pick a spacing (gap map suggests one Full every 3-4 layers) and state the KV-cache bytes saved per token at each spacing.
3. m (tokens per entry): start value in 4..8 for seq 4096, with the cache arithmetic.
4. Indexer geometry dividing h=8 and d=1024: indexer heads, indexer head dim, core latent dim. Gap map suggests 4 x 64 and latent d//4=256; confirm.
5. Attention top-k entries per query for seq 4096: a value in 64..128, with the calculation showing it is NOT effectively dense (top-k * m << seq).
6. n_win: pick 128 or keep 256 for the initial build; the 128-vs-256 A/B is a later task, you only need a default.
Report per-token global KV bytes for the chosen config and compare it head-on to a dense 4096 KV at the same width — that number is the reason this architecture exists.
GREEN: scripts/v41_size.py builds both configs on torch.device("meta") and prints active params (the repo lesson: count, do not assume), and every chosen value appears as a Cfg field with a comment naming it a small-scale re-choice, not a paper value.
reading: green means every number is re-derived for d=1024/h=8/seq4096 with the arithmetic shown, every knob is a Cfg field, and the per-token KV saving is stated rather than implied. A value copied from the paper's 552B config is a fail
produces: scripts/v41_size.py and Cfg defaults for L/CSA2 mode map/m/indexer-geometry/top-k/n_win, each with the small-scale arithmetic and a per-token KV byte figure vs dense
decides: the config de-103 builds against; it blocks de's Cfg fields

task: V4.1 Step 2: CSA2 Full/Reuse cross-layer KV package through the model body
why:
WHAT: V4.1 Step 2 — cross-layer Full/Reuse KV package for CSA2, threaded through HybridLM._body. Depends on de-103 (CSA2 core) and ae-2 (the mode map); start after de's module interface is settled, you can design against it now.
WHY: user order 2026-09-10 V2 -> DeepSeek-V4.1. This is the layer-dimension KV sharing that replaces HCA and carries most of CSA2's cache saving.
BUILD (Sec 2.3.1, Fig.4; config in docs/standards/v41_pivot.md):
1. Static per-layer mode list from Cfg (ae-2 produces it). Each CSA2 layer is Full, Reuse, or (later, not now) Reindex.
2. A Full layer emits a package: learned entries C, weights Z, indexer-K, and the top-k selection indices, plus block/visibility metadata. A Reuse layer consumes that package and owns ONLY its own main Q and its own layer-local SWA KV — it does not materialize global K/V or run the indexer.
3. Thread the package alongside x through the body. Keep every layer's own SWA KV from its own H_l (paper keeps SWA strictly layer-wise even in the decoder).
4. Do NOT build Reindex — in V4.1 it exists only in the decoder half, and we are building flat CSA2 first. Structure the package so Reindex can be added without a rewrite.
TESTS (these are the acceptance, not just nice-to-have): a Reuse layer's output must CHANGE when its source Full layer's KV package changes, and must NOT change when a neighbouring Reuse layer's parameters change; and a Reuse layer adds zero global-branch parameters of its own. Reuse must still respect causal and per-document masking inherited from the package's block metadata.
reading: green means the three tests above pass: source-change propagates, neighbour-change does not, Reuse adds no global KV params; and SWA KV stays strictly per-layer. Depends on de-103's interface and ae-2's mode map, so coordinate before coding
produces: a Full-emits/Reuse-consumes package plumbed through the body, with the dependency and zero-extra-params tests passing
decides: how much KV is actually shared across layers — the cache-saving half of CSA2

task: V4.1 Step 3: pure-SWA block + configurable first-N SWA-only layer placement
why:
WHAT: V4.1 Step 3 — a pure-SWA attention block and configurable placement so the first N blocks (paper: first two) can be SWA-only with no global CSA2 branch. Your frozen 0e-1 exercise generator stays frozen; this is the new priority.
WHY: user order 2026-09-10 V2 -> DeepSeek-V4.1. In V4.1 every layer has a local SWA branch and layers 0-1 are SWA-only (Sec 2.1, config Sec 4.2.1 n_win=128 at 552B).
BUILD:
1. A pure-SWA attention module: local window keys + per-document mask only, no global/CSA2 branch. The window mask code already exists inside CompressedSparseAttention (model.py:489-492 unpacked, 531-534 packed); extract/reuse it, do not re-write the mask.
2. A Cfg placement field (e.g. n_swa_only_layers, default 2) so HybridLM builds the first blocks pure-SWA and the rest CSA2; make it compose with the mode map ae-2 produces.
3. Parameterise n_win (default per ae-2; paper 128, current code csa_window=256) so the 128-vs-256 A/B is a config change, not a code change.
4. Test: SWA-only block attends only within window and within document; a token outside the window is invisible; finite output on an all-masked row.
Coordinate with de (de-103) since you both touch the attention module — branch from the same base, do not conflict on model.py; announce on the file.
reading: green means: outside-window and cross-document tokens are provably invisible, all-masked rows stay finite, and the placement composes with ae-2's CSA2 mode map. Reuse the existing window mask rather than re-writing it
produces: a pure-SWA attention option with an n_swa_only_layers placement field and per-document window tests

task: V4.1 Step 1: implement CSA2 core in a flat stack (learned entries + dedicated indexer + single concatenated softmax)
why:
WHAT: Implement CSA2 core in a FLAT stack behind a csa2 flag — Step 1 of docs/standards/v41_pivot.md (PR #210). This is the central mechanism of the new target and the first gate candidate; everything else waits on it.
WHY: user order 2026-09-10 replaced V2 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. V2 PR #206 is dead, do not merge it.
BUILD (from a full-read gap map against model.py, verified):
1. Rewrite CompressedSparseAttention (model.py:381-538). CSA2 = (a) learned non-overlapping m-token KV entries with a learned projection producing entries C and per-entry weights Z, REPLACING the mean-pool in pool_per_doc (model.py:277-318 — keep its block/visibility/per-document machinery, change only the aggregation to a learned entry); (b) a DEDICATED lightweight indexer: indexer-Q Linear from H, indexer-K Linear over the compressed entries (not H), low-dim scores -> top-k entry indices per query; (c) gather those entries and run ONE concatenated softmax over [selected entries ; local SWA window K/V]. DELETE branch_gate, the y_sel full-resolution gather, and the separate y_cmp softmax — V4.1 has no branch gate (Fig 4, Sec 2.3).
2. Reuse the existing cu per-document isolation, blk_last<=t visibility, masked_attend, and the all-masked-row handling. Extend scripts/test_arch_compat.py with causality and cross-document cases for the indexer path; indexer top-k must never select a future or cross-document entry.
3. Geometry at OUR width, do NOT copy 552B: paper uses 32 indexer-Q heads x dim 128 against 64 core heads x dim 512 at latent 1280 (Sec 4.2.1). At d=1024/h=8 derive values that divide evenly — gap-map suggestion indexer 4 heads x 64 dim, core latent d//4=256 — but put them in Cfg and record the choice; this is a Step-0 config decision and I want your numbers.
4. Start m=4..8 and top-k 64..128 for seq 4096 (paper m=2/1, top-k 512 are for 64K-1M; at 4K top-k 512 over m=8 entries is dense attention in disguise). A/B later; one value to start.
5. No CED, no Reindex, no FP4, no bounded replay in this task — flat stack only. SWA branch already exists; pure-SWA-first-two-blocks is a separate task.
GREEN: a config builds and runs a forward+backward on meta then real tensors with csa2=true; the three invariant classes (causal, per-document, finite-on-all-masked-row) pass; a dedicated test proves the indexer mask cannot leak future/cross-doc entries. Reference is the paper text in docs/standards/v41_pivot.md and the PDF at /Users/bytedance/Downloads/DeepSeek_V41_Tech_Report.pdf Sec 2.3.

task: V4.1 Step 2: CSA2 Full/Reuse cross-layer KV package through the model body
why:
WHAT: V4.1 Step 2 — cross-layer Full/Reuse KV package for CSA2, threaded through HybridLM._body. Depends on de-103 (CSA2 core) and ae-2 (the mode map); start after de's module interface is settled, you can design against it now.
WHY: user order 2026-09-10 V2 -> DeepSeek-V4.1. This is the layer-dimension KV sharing that replaces HCA and carries most of CSA2's cache saving.
BUILD (Sec 2.3.1, Fig.4; config in docs/standards/v41_pivot.md):
1. Static per-layer mode list from Cfg (ae-2 produces it). Each CSA2 layer is Full, Reuse, or (later, not now) Reindex.
2. A Full layer emits a package: learned entries C, weights Z, indexer-K, and the top-k selection indices, plus block/visibility metadata. A Reuse layer consumes that package and owns ONLY its own main Q and its own layer-local SWA KV — it does not materialize global K/V or run the indexer.
3. Thread the package alongside x through the body. Keep every layer's own SWA KV from its own H_l (paper keeps SWA strictly layer-wise even in the decoder).
4. Do NOT build Reindex — in V4.1 it exists only in the decoder half, and we are building flat CSA2 first. Structure the package so Reindex can be added without a rewrite.
TESTS (these are the acceptance, not just nice-to-have): a Reuse layer's output must CHANGE when its source Full layer's KV package changes, and must NOT change when a neighbouring Reuse layer's parameters change; and a Reuse layer adds zero global-branch parameters of its own. Reuse must still respect causal and per-document masking inherited from the package's block metadata.
reading: green means the three tests above pass: source-change propagates, neighbour-change does not, Reuse adds no global KV params; and SWA KV stays strictly per-layer. Depends on de-103's interface and ae-2's mode map, so coordinate before coding
produces: a Full-emits/Reuse-consumes package plumbed through the body, with the dependency and zero-extra-params tests passing
decides: how much KV is actually shared across layers — the cache-saving half of CSA2
drop_reason: CSA2 Full/Reuse package is in model.py and exercised by smoke g/i/j; delivered

Nothing was claimed.' The measurement completed and read 1.0000 -- correct numbers, zero claim -- and a peer reading nvidia-smi and the ledger at 00:5xZ correctly saw an idle card with no claim while the run had already happened. Fix the shape, not that one run: --wait-for-device exists for a LAUNCHER following torchrun onto a card, where the job outlives the poll; a self-claiming short job needs a different mechanism. The workaround that worked is a python wrapper holding the claim in its own pid across the whole measurement (python because card_claim refuses a shell), which is 20 lines every short job must re-derive.
why: A claim ledger that a whole class of jobs silently escapes is worse than one that refuses them: idle-is-not-a-grant is enforced by reading claims, so an unclaimed run makes a card look free while it is in use, and the next session's launch is the collision. The class is not rare -- every score_matrix row, every micro-timing, every known-answer test on a card is seconds to minutes, i.e. shorter than the poll. The failure is silent in the direction that matters (it prints a note and exits 0), so nobody discovers it until two jobs land on one card.
